results.summary_before: This is a RISC-V SoC called KianV uLinux that can boot a small Linux system, implemented in Verilog across an 8x2 tile area. It provides a UART interface, SPI connections for flash and PSRAM, and several LED outputs, with one bidirectional pin held always high. The design is notable for being a full Linux-capable RISC-V ASIC on a Tiny Tapeout shuttle. External hardware includes SPI flash and PSRAM memories, and the documentation is limited to pin names without detailed usage instructions.

results.summary_before: This design is a nibble-serial implementation of the LED block cipher, which encrypts a 64-bit plaintext block using a 128-bit key. It serializes both data input and output to fit within the limited I/O pins, controlled by a simple handshake protocol. The cipher requires external hardware, such as a Raspberry Pi, to provide the serial data and control signals. The design is notable for its compact implementation, reusing datapath logic across nibbles, at the cost of increased latency.

results.summary_before: This project is an 8-bit prefix network-based adder designed with the aid of a large language model to achieve a balance between power, performance, and area. It takes two 8-bit operands (a and b) and produces an 8-bit sum output. The design uses specific modules (Square, BigCircle, SmallCircle, Triangle) to generate carries and sums. The test procedure applies all possible input combinations and verifies the sum against the expected result, ensuring correct functionality.
